turns.a_html:
A quick note first: I'm not a licensed investment advisor. What follows is research and a valuation framework, not a buy or sell recommendation. Decide for yourself.

Bottom line

It's a good company, but at about $51–53 the price is not cheap. Today's price assumes Neutron eventually works. My rough probability-weighted fair value is around $35–40. The stock still trades above that even after a 20% drop in one week.

1. Competition

Area Rocket Lab's position Main rivals Assessment
Small launch (Electron/HASTE) Clear #1 in the West; launch backlog of 90+ missions SpaceX rideshare (much cheaper per kg), Firefly Alpha A moat, but a small market. HASTE hypersonic testing for the military is the highlight
Medium launch (Neutron) Hasn't flown. Slipped from 2024 → 2025 → late 2026 → 2027 SpaceX Falcon 9 (dominant, listed, about $1.8T market cap); New Glenn (has flown but its pad blew up in May); Firefly Eclipse, Stoke Nova, Relativity Terran R (all targeting 2027) Being late hurts less than it sounds, because every newcomer has slipped. Whoever reliably flies first becomes the "second supplier" behind SpaceX
Satellites and components (Space Systems, about 75% of revenue) Becoming a defense prime: SDA Tranche 2 plus Tranche 3 ($805M); bought Geost (infrared payloads) Northrop, L3Harris, Lockheed, York This is the most underrated part. It earns revenue now and has a moat in vertical integration
Satellite communications (after the Iridium acquisition) $8B purchase, expected to close mid-2027 Starlink direct-to-cell, AST SpaceMobile Adds steady cash flow, but Starlink puts long-term pressure on Iridium's niche

2. Fundamentals

  • Q2 2026: revenue $234M (+62% year on year), backlog $2.36B (+137%), net loss $49M. Q3 guidance is $250–265M, and results come out 11/9.
  • Cash: about $2.4B on hand, but free cash flow was about −$110M per quarter. Much of the cash is reserved for Iridium's cash portion ($27 per share), with a $3.6B bridge loan on top.
  • Dilution: ATM share sales raised about $1.5B in the first half. The Iridium stock portion and the Geost shares add more. The share count is heading toward roughly 700M.
  • The CFO has said cash flow improves only after Neutron's first flight. That is now pushed back about two quarters, so burn lasts longer and more share sales are possible.

3. Valuation (rough, 2030 numbers discounted back at 12%)

Market cap is about $30–33B. Pro forma 2027 revenue including Iridium is about $2.3B, so EV/Sales is about 14x.

Scenario 2030 revenue Multiple (EV/Sales) Per share (2030) Discounted to today
Bear: Neutron slips again or flies rarely $3B 4x ~$14 ~$10
Base: Neutron flies in 2027, about 15 launches/yr by 2030 $5B 7x ~$48 ~$33
Bull: reuse works, becomes a true #2 $7B 10x ~$100 ~$69

Weighting these 25/50/25 gives about $36. At $51 the market is pricing the base case or better.

4. Price levels (from the chart and the valuation)

Recent prices: the 52-week low is $37.57 (11/21/2025). The base from November–December 2025 was $40–45. $58–60 (the July low, also yesterday's breakdown point) is now resistance. $66–70 is heavy overhead supply.

If you buy in steps, the way you do with ARGX, a valuation-based reference ladder would be:

  • ~$45: first tranche, light. This is the November 2025 consolidation zone, about a 25% premium to the base case.
  • ~$40: main tranche, close to the base-case value plus the bottom of the prior range.
  • ~$35: add, below base-case value, with a margin of safety.

Above $50 I would not chase; it isn't priced attractively. If it never comes down that far, missing it is fine.

5. When: watch the triggers, not the calendar

  1. 11/9, Q3 results: check the Q4 guidance, whether Neutron's cost is raised, the free-cash-flow trend, and whether a new ATM is announced. A delay is often followed by a second leg down, so waiting until after results costs little.
  2. Q1 2027: Neutron cryogenic and hydrostatic tests finish. Passing them is the first hard signal.
  3. Mid-2027: Iridium closes. Check the final dilution and debt.
  4. Neutron's first flight: success re-rates the stock, but by then it will no longer be cheap.

Thesis-breakers: Neutron fails a test again or slips past the end of 2027; Space Systems gross margin falls; dilution keeps running above about 10% a year.

Things I couldn't fully confirm

  • The cash balance comes from secondary summaries. Check the 10-Q.
  • Today's intraday quotes vary between $50.7 and $53.6. Check live before acting.
  • I haven't confirmed how the Iridium collar ($67.50–$112.50) works when RKLB trades below $67.50, so I don't know whether the exchange ratio stays fixed.

Sources: 24/7 Wall St. on the Neutron delay · Investing.com · Q2 press release · Spaceflight Now · Iridium deal · ATM replacement program · SDA Tranche 3 · SpaceX IPO · Firefly Eclipse · Stoke funding · New Glenn explosion · Robinhood quote · Price history: akshare (Sina source)
